With core AI features built in, you get help prepping for meetings, taking meeting notes with My notes, catching up on messages you missed, and drafting content faster. 

GET MORE DONE ON THE GO WITH ZOOM AI*
Built-in AI notetaker for AI-generated meeting summaries
Draft messages and content with AI that knows your work context
Catch up on unread Chat messages in seconds

ONE APP FOR VIDEO CONFERENCING, CHAT, AND CALLS
Schedule or join a video meeting with one tap
Send messages to colleagues and external contacts in Team Chat
Place and receive phone calls or send SMS text messages with Zoom Phone*

BOOST YOUR PRODUCTIVITY
Create and share Zoom Docs to keep your team aligned
Get automatic meeting summaries
Brainstorm and collaborate on Zoom Whiteboard

SWITCH BETWEEN DEVICES WITHOUT MISSING A BEAT
Move a live video call or phone call between devices with one tap
Start a Zoom Rooms meeting and share your screen*

WORK SAFELY ON THE GO

Keep your data protected with enterprise-grade security and SSO*

quotes.text:
I don't want to live in a world where my parents and grandparents are expected to pull up Wireshark to figure out if the app they're using will record their front camera without consent.

Blaming Zoom and FB is entirely acceptable here, it is their responsibility to keep my data private.

Blaming Apple? Why, when Zoom is on the Play Store as well?

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=us.zoom.videomeetings&hl=en

>As long as you're running binary blobs that can make whatever network connections they please, people are going to take your data and send it to places you don't know about.

Surely there are open source video chat solutions already? They haven't taken off for one simple reason: video hosting is expensive. It's quite literally one of the most intensive network activities you can partake in, rivaling torrenting.

It doesn't make sense economically to offer a video hosting platform without collecting income from it. Nor does it make sense to attempt a peer-to-peer solution knowing full well that one laggy peer wrecks the experience for everyone else.

It's a very hard problem.
quotes.story_title: Zoom’s Use of Facebook’s SDK in iOS Client
